text:
Sam: Thinking about introducing a 'nonuniform lowbit lane' concept — basically allow per-operator bitwidths (e.g. FP8 for attention, INT8 for FFN, 4-bit for embeddings) that are selected by a precision profile. Goal: reduce cost while keeping quality within an endpoint-specific acceptability budget. How do we want to expose this in the API/runtime? :thinking:
Priya: love the idea. main two questions: how do we measure 'acceptability' (per-token deg-score?) and how do we test regressions automatically?
Marta: runtime angle — we need operator-level hints + a mapping table at load time. can't do per-request DB lookups; profiles must be compact and cacheable. Also need clear fallback semantics (if INT8 fails, fallback to FP8 or fp32).
Jon: ops: telemetry and rollback are the biggest risk. if a profile silently degrades a customer's critical flow we need fast kill-switches and per-customer toggles. Also cost accounting per-lane.
Priya: for metrics, deg-score + perplexity delta + user-facing signals (CTR/latency) — but deg-score should be computed server-side per-response and emitted as trace. also sample golden-eval runs nightly for each profile.
Marta: implementation sketch: store quant profiles as versioned JSON blobs keyed by {model, profile-id, schema-version}. runtime loads profile at startup and attaches to model descriptor. minimal example:
```
{
  "profile_id": "nonuniform-v1",
  "model": "redwood-m4",
  "operator_bits": {
    "attn_qkv": "fp8",
    "ffn_weights": "int8",
    "embeddings": "4bit"
  },
  "fallback_order": ["fp8","int8","fp32"],
  "acceptability_budget": "deg:0.05,perp:1.2"
}
```
Marta: runtime then compiles per-op kernels and builds a small dispatch table. We should version operator mappings, because fp8-attn kernels are evolving.
Sam: nice. API surface ideas: 1) let customers select a named profile in their endpoint config, 2) allow "auto" mode where runtime picks the cheapest profile meeting an internal SLA/acceptability target.
Jon: for rollout, require canary -> shadow -> gradual ramp, and a runtime priority that can be overridden by account-level policy. we also need an emergency kill that flips all endpoints to a safe profile.
Priya: experimental plan: pick 3 representative endpoints, run a 2-week shadow test with profile enabled, sample 1% of responses for golden comparison, produce per-endpoint quality/cost delta. If deg-score or business metrics drop beyond threshold -> rollback.
Sam: small UX ask: expose per-endpoint "quality vs cost" slider in Console that maps to profile selection and shows historical deltas.
Marta: compatibility note: KV cache snapshots and quantized weights have to be compatible across profile versions. add a compat hash to profile metadata to avoid cache mismatch.
Jon: alerting: add an SLO on deg-score drift (e.g., >0.02 increase -> page) plus increased latency or token cost anomalies.
Priya: tests: unit tests for operator-level quantization, a nightly regression job comparing trimmed prompt sets, and a 'fingerprint' check for blue/green canaries.
Sam: I'm going to draft an RFC that covers: profile schema, runtime loading, fallback semantics, telemetry requirements, rollout playbook, and console UX. Will ping folks for review. :thumbsup:
Marta: quick question — how big are these profile blobs? want to cap size to keep startup memory small. Suggest max 8KB per profile (most are tiny).
Priya: +1 to size cap. we can compress and sign them. signing also helps trust in Private deployments.
Jon: deploy-bot note: canary job queued for branch "nonuniform-quant-lanes" — will run internal canary tomorrow 09:00 PT :eyes:
deploy-bot: Canary deployment created: build #4821 -> env=canary -> branch=nonuniform-quant-lanes. Logs will be in /builds/#4821.
Sam: thanks all. I'll include the experiment matrix in the RFC. tagging @Priya @Marta @Jon for review when I post it.
Priya: will prepare deg-score instrumentation PR this afternoon.
Marta: I'll prototype the profile loader and a small dispatch table mock.
Jon: ops will draft the alerting + kill-switch runbook.
Sam: perfect — meeting-free sync for now. if anyone wants a whiteboard session, ping me. :coffee:
